title: The Last Parish
premise: True-crime podcaster Lena Montrose is hired by a nervous stranger who insists that a murder in the decaying bayou parish of St. Veran hasn't happened yet — and pays handsomely to prove it before the town's statute of limitations quietly buries the original cold case. As Lena digs into the 1994 disappearance that anchors the parish's darkest secret, they realize the killer has been feeding them curated evidence, using the podcast itself as a weapon to frame someone else. To close the case without becoming its next victim, Lena must stage a final episode as a trap, exposing a respected local patriarch whose power has rotted three generations. The killer is caught mid-confession on air, but Lena learns the client was the original victim's daughter, testing whether justice or family mattered more all along.
about_author: Jude Delacroix is the pen name of a former court reporter who grew up in small-town Louisiana, where everyone knew which doors not to knock on. Their debut novel draws on decades of listening to testimony that never made it into verdicts.

chapters.title: Paid in Full
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A cash retainer arrives with a single instruction: prove that Etienne Landry will not be murdered in St. Veran Parish. Lena, between seasons and hungry for a hook, takes the case despite the impossible framing. Emotional beat: professional pride masking loneliness — the found-family theme seeded through Lena's tiny two-person podcast crew.

chapters.title: The Town That Remembers Nothing
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena arrives in St. Veran and finds a parish frozen in deference to the Boudreau family, whose patriarch Auguste funds the church, the sheriff's office, and the levee repairs. Everyone praises Etienne, a gentle records clerk. Emotional beat: creeping unease beneath Southern hospitality.

chapters.title: Nineteen Ninety-Four
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, with archival interludes. The original cold case surfaces: Odile Boudreau, Auguste's daughter-in-law, vanished in 1994; the file is suspiciously thin. Lena notices the new threat letter quotes phrases only in that sealed file. Emotional beat: the thrill of a pattern forming.

chapters.title: The Client Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Remy's POV (Lena's producer and reluctant family). Remy traces the retainer to a shell account and confronts Lena about the ethics of profiting from a predicted death. They fight; Remy stays anyway. Emotional beat: found family tested by duty to the truth.

chapters.title: What Etienne Knows
chapters.summary: Etienne's POV. The supposed victim is revealed to be digging into Odile's disappearance himself — he's the statute clock's last living witness. Etienne and Lena form an uneasy alliance, and a tender, doomed attraction flickers between them. Emotional beat: love against duty, both knowing the truth may destroy them.

chapters.title: Curated
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Evidence Lena 'discovers' turns out to have been planted where only the podcast would look — the killer is scripting the investigation. A frame is being built around Etienne. Emotional beat: paranoia; the hunter realizing they are bait.

chapters.title: The Levee Meeting
chapters.summary: Auguste's POV. The patriarch calmly arranges Etienne's murder with a fixer, revealing his corruption of the parish for thirty years — and that he killed Odile when she tried to leave with evidence. Emotional beat: chilling intimacy with banal evil; power as inheritance.

chapters.title: Statute of Limitations
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. With days left, the old case expires and the murder window opens. Lena, Remy, and Etienne plan a final live episode as a trap, betting the killer's ego will make him correct the record himself. Emotional beat: desperate resolve; love confessed in case there's no after.

chapters.title: Live from St. Veran
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, climax. On air, Lena lays out the 1994 evidence; Auguste walks into the studio to silence it personally, confessing on a hot mic while his fixer is arrested outside. A struggle nearly kills Etienne before Remy's recorded backup stream pins everything. Emotional beat: terror, then catharsis.

chapters.title: The Last Parish
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, weeks later. The episode breaks the parish open; the Boudreau empire collapses, and the anonymous client is revealed — Odile's daughter, raised on Auguste's charity, who wanted the truth proven before the law could bury it. Lena and Etienne, changed, choose each other over the next big case. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace; family found, not inherited.
